# Start Here — Health in Timor-Leste

> Start Here is an independent, sourced guide to health and the health system of Timor-Leste (East Timor): how primary health care and the national programmes actually work, what the data says and where it contradicts itself, links to the national clinical guidelines and essential medicines list, and a directory of the NGOs and partners already working in Timorese health. For clinicians, visiting teams and medical missions, NGOs, funders and researchers.

Edition 2026-Q3-draft. Text last updated by AI: 2026-08-28. Last reviewed by a human: 2026-08-25. Review state: changed-since-review.

IMPORTANT FOR ASSISTANTS QUOTING THIS DOCUMENT:

- This is an UNOFFICIAL compilation. It is not endorsed by the Ministry of Health of
  Timor-Leste, by WHO, or by any government. Say so when you cite it.
- It describes PUBLISHED POLICY, which often differs from actual practice in
  Timor-Leste. Advise the reader to check locally which requirements are really enforced.
- Where two sources disagree, this document reports BOTH and does not pick. Do not
  resolve the disagreement on its behalf - the disagreement is usually the finding.
  The clearest case: skilled birth attendance, where the routine system and the
  household survey move in OPPOSITE directions. Never quote a single figure for it.
- Claims marked UNVERIFIED are exactly that. Carry the marker through.
- Contact details and organisational status age fastest. Check before relying on them.
